title: 3Sum Closest
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer target, find three integers in nums such that their sum is as close as possible to target.

Return the sum of those three integers. You may assume that each input has exactly one such sum.
constraints_html:
• 3 <= nums.length <= 500
  • -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000
  • -10^4 <= target <= 10^4

title: Alien Dictionary
statement_html:
There is a new alien language that uses the English alphabet, but the order among the letters is unknown. You are given a list of words from this language's dictionary, where the words are sorted lexicographically according to the rules of this new language.

Derive one valid ordering of the letters in this language based on the given words, and return it as a string with no separators. If the given words are not a valid sort under any possible letter ordering (including a word appearing before a proper prefix of itself, or a cyclic contradiction), return an empty string "".
constraints_html:
• 1 <= words.length <= 100
  • 1 <= words[i].length <= 100
  • words[i] consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Assign Cookies
statement_html:
You are given an array g where g[i] is the minimum cookie size that will content the i-th child, and an array s where s[j] is the size of the j-th cookie.

Each cookie can be given to at most one child, and a child is content only if the cookie they receive has size greater than or equal to their greed factor. Give out cookies to maximize the number of content children.

Return the maximum number of children you can make content.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= g.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • 0 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • 1 <= g[i], s[j] <= 2^31 - 1

title: Asteroid Collision
statement_html:
You are given an array of integers asteroids representing asteroids lined up in a row.

For each asteroid, the absolute value represents its size, and the sign represents its direction (positive means moving right, negative means moving left). Every asteroid moves at the same speed.

When two asteroids meet, the smaller one explodes. If both are the same size, both explode. Two asteroids moving in the same direction will never meet.

Return the state of the asteroids after all collisions have finished.
constraints_html:
• 2 <= asteroids.length <= 10^4
  • -1000 <= asteroids[i] <= 1000
  • asteroids[i] != 0

title: Backspace String Compare
statement_html: Given two strings s and t, return true if they would be equal when both are typed into empty text editors. The character # represents a backspace, which deletes the previous character (if any).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 200
  • s and t only contain lowercase letters and the character #.

title: Basic Calculator
statement_html:
Given a string s representing a valid arithmetic expression, implement a basic calculator to evaluate and return its value.

The expression may contain non-negative integers, the operators + and -, parentheses ( and ), and spaces. You do not need to support * or /, and you may not use eval().
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^5
  • s consists of digits, +, -, (, ), and spaces
  • s is a valid expression

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
statement_html:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on day i.

Unlike the single-transaction version of this problem, you may buy and sell the stock as many times as you like, as long as you sell before buying again (you may hold at most one share at a time). Return the maximum total profit you can achieve.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= prices.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
statement_html:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most two transactions.

Note that you cannot engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (you must sell the stock before you buy again).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= prices.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
statement_html:
You are given an integer k and an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most k transactions: that is, you may buy at most k times and sell at most k times.

Note that you cannot engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (you must sell the stock before you buy again).
constraints_html:
• 0 <= k <= 100
  • 0 <= prices.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
statement_html:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete as many transactions as you like (buy one and sell one share of the stock multiple times) subject to the following restrictions:

After you sell your stock, you cannot buy stock on the next day (i.e., a cooldown of one day is required). You may not engage in multiple transactions at the same time (you must sell the stock before you buy again).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= prices.length <= 5000
  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement_html:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on day i.

You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy the stock and a different day in the future to sell it. Return the maximum profit you can achieve, or 0 if no profit is possible.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= prices.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4

title: Binary Search
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums sorted in ascending order, with all elements distinct, and an integer target.

Write a function that searches for target in nums. If it exists, return its index; otherwise return -1.

You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^4 < nums[i], target < 10^4
  • All the integers in nums are unique
  • nums is sorted in ascending order

title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
statement_html:
Given two integers left and right that represent an inclusive range [left, right], return the bitwise AND of every number in that range.

Since the range can contain up to 2^31 numbers, computing this by iterating over every value can be far too slow for large ranges — look for a way to determine the common binary prefix shared by left and right instead.
constraints_html: • 0 <= left <= right <= 2^31 - 1

title: Boats to Save People
statement_html:
You are given an array people where people[i] is the weight of the i-th person, and an integer limit denoting the maximum weight a single boat can carry.

Each boat carries at most two people at once, as long as the sum of their weights does not exceed limit. Return the minimum number of boats needed to carry everyone across.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= people.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • 1 <= people[i] <= limit <= 3 * 10^4

title: Candy
statement_html:
There are n children standing in a line, each assigned a rating value given in the array ratings. You must give each child at least one candy.

Any child with a strictly higher rating than either of their immediate neighbors must receive more candies than that neighbor.

Return the minimum total number of candies you need to distribute to satisfy these requirements.
constraints_html:
• n == ratings.length
  • 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
  • 0 <= ratings[i] <= 2 * 10^4

title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
statement_html:
A conveyor belt has packages, given as an array weights, that must be shipped from one port to another within days days, in the same order that they appear in the array.

Each day, the ship loads packages (in order) onto itself, up to its maximum weight capacity, then departs. Once a package is loaded it cannot be split across days.

Return the least weight capacity of the ship that will allow all the packages to be shipped within days days.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= days <= weights.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • 1 <= weights[i] <= 500

title: Car Fleet
statement_html:
There are n cars traveling to the same destination on a one-lane road, located at coordinate target.

You are given two arrays, position and speed, both of length n, where position[i] is the starting position of the i-th car and speed[i] is its speed. All cars move toward target and never change speed on their own.

If a car catches up to the car in front of it, they travel together as a single fleet at the speed of the slower (front) car, from then on staying together.

Return the number of distinct fleets that arrive at the destination.
constraints_html:
• n == position.length == speed.length
  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 < target <= 10^6
  • 0 <= position[i] < target
  • All values of position are unique
  • 0 < speed[i] <= 10^6

title: Car Pooling
statement_html:
Your car has a fixed number of empty seats given by capacity. You are given a list of trips, trips, where trips[i] = [numPassengers_i, from_i, to_i] means that numPassengers_i passengers must be picked up at road position from_i and dropped off at road position to_i (all positions are non-negative, and the car only ever travels in one direction of increasing position).

Return true if it is possible to pick up and drop off every trip's passengers without ever exceeding capacity at any point along the route, otherwise return false.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= trips.length <= 1000
  • 1 <= numPassengers_i <= 100
  • 0 <= from_i < to_i <= 1000
  • 1 <= capacity <= 10^5

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
statement_html:
There are n cities numbered from 0 to n - 1, connected by flights given as flights[i] = [from_i, to_i, price_i], meaning there is a flight from city from_i to city to_i costing price_i.

Given src, dst, and k, return the cheapest price to travel from src to dst using at most k stops (intermediate cities), or -1 if no such route exists.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 100
  • 0 <= flights.length <= (n * (n - 1)) / 2
  • 0 <= from_i, to_i < n
  • 1 <= price_i <= 10^4
  • 0 <= src, dst, k < n
  • src != dst

title: Cherry Pickup
statement_html:
You are given an n x n grid grid where each cell has one of three values:

  • 0 - an empty cell you can walk through.
  • 1 - a cell containing a cherry that can be picked up.
  • -1 - a cell containing a thorn that blocks any path.

    • Starting at the top-left cell (0, 0), you make one trip to the bottom-right cell (n - 1, n - 1) moving only right or down, collecting any cherries along the way (a cell's cherry can only be collected once). Then you make a second trip, moving only left or up, back to (0, 0), again collecting any remaining cherries.

    Return the maximum number of cherries that can be collected using both trips combined. If there is no valid path from (0, 0) to (n - 1, n - 1) and back, return 0.
constraints_html:
• n == grid.length == grid[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 50
  • grid[i][j] is -1, 0, or 1.
  • grid[0][0] != -1 and grid[n - 1][n - 1] != -1.

title: Climbing Stairs
statement_html:
You are climbing a staircase that takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps.

In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 45

title: Coin Change II
statement_html:
You are given an integer amount and an array coins representing different coin denominations. You have an infinite number of coins of each denomination.

Return the number of distinct combinations of coins that sum up to amount. Two combinations are the same if they use the same coins with the same counts, regardless of order. If no combination makes up amount, return 0.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= coins.length <= 300
  • 1 <= coins[i] <= 5000
  • All values in coins are unique.
  • 0 <= amount <= 5000

title: Coin Change
statement_html:
You are given an array of integers coins representing coin denominations, and an integer amount representing a target sum of money.

Return the fewest number of coins needed to make up amount, using any number of coins of each denomination. If it's impossible to make amount with the given coins, return -1.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= coins.length <= 12
  • 1 <= coins[i] <= 2^31 - 1
  • 0 <= amount <= 10^4

title: Combination Sum II
statement_html:
Given a collection of integers candidates (which may contain duplicates) and a target integer target, return every unique combination of numbers from candidates that add up to target.

Each number in candidates may be used at most once per combination (each index may be picked only once, even though the same value can appear at multiple indices). The result must not contain duplicate combinations — you may return the combinations (and the numbers within each) in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= candidates.length <= 100
  • 1 <= candidates[i] <= 50
  • 1 <= target <= 30

title: Combination Sum IV
statement_html:
Given an array of distinct positive integers nums and a target integer target, return the number of possible ordered sequences that add up to target. Numbers may be reused as many times as needed.

Different orderings of the same numbers count as different sequences.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 200
  • All elements of nums are distinct positive integers.
  • 1 <= target <= 1000

title: Combination Sum
statement_html:
Given an array of distinct positive integers candidates and a target integer target, return every unique combination of numbers from candidates that add up to target.

The same number may be chosen from candidates an unlimited number of times within one combination. Two combinations are considered the same if they use the same numbers the same number of times, regardless of order — you may return the combinations (and the numbers within each) in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= candidates.length <= 30
  • 2 <= candidates[i] <= 40
  • All elements of candidates are distinct.
  • 1 <= target <= 40

title: Compare Version Numbers
statement_html:
A version number is a string containing one or more revisions, each made up of digits, separated by dots '.'. Each revision's numeric value is formed by dropping any leading zeros; a revision that is missing entirely (past the end of a shorter version string) is treated as 0.

Given two version strings version1 and version2, compare them by their revisions in order. Return -1 if version1 < version2, 1 if version1 > version2, and 0 if they are equal.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= version1.length, version2.length <= 500
  • Each version string consists of digits and dots '.'.
  • Every revision contains at least one digit, and the numeric value of every revision fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Container With Most Water
statement_html:
You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of the i-th line are (i, 0) and (i, height[i]).

Find two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container that holds the most water, and return the maximum amount of water it can store.

Note: the container cannot be slanted; it is formed only by two vertical lines and the x-axis.
constraints_html:
• 2 <= height.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 10^4

title: Contains Duplicate
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums, determine whether any value appears at least twice in the array.

Return true if any value appears more than once, and return false if every element is distinct.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums has a contiguous subarray of size at least two whose elements sum to a multiple of k, or false otherwise.

A sum that is a multiple of k means there exists an integer n such that the subarray's sum equals n * k. Note that n = 0 is valid, so a subarray summing to 0 always counts as a multiple of any k.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
  • 0 <= sum(nums[i]) <= 2^31 - 1
  • 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1

title: Count and Say
statement_html:
The count-and-say sequence starts with "1". Each following term is generated by reading off the previous term: for each run of the same digit, write the number of times it repeats, then the digit itself.

For example, "1" is read as "one 1" → "11", which is read as "two 1s" → "21", which is read as "one 2, one 1" → "1211".

Given a positive integer n, return the nth term of this sequence as a string.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 30

title: Counting Bits
statement_html:
Given an integer n, return an array ans of length n + 1 where ans[i] is the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of i, for every i from 0 to n.

Try to come up with a solution that runs in O(n) total time, ideally by reusing previously computed answers instead of recomputing each bit count from scratch.
constraints_html: • 0 <= n <= 10^5

title: Course Schedule
statement_html:
There are numCourses courses labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means you must take course b before course a.

Return true if it is possible to finish all courses, or false if the prerequisites form a cycle that makes it impossible.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= numCourses <= 2000
  • 0 <= prerequisites.length <= 5000
  • prerequisites[i].length == 2
  • All pairs [a, b] are distinct.

title: Critical Connections in a Network
statement_html:
There are n servers numbered from 0 to n - 1 connected by undirected server-to-server connections, forming a network. Each connections[i] = [a, b] represents a connection between servers a and b.

A critical connection (also called a bridge) is a connection that, if removed, would split the network into two or more disconnected components. Return all critical connections in the network, in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 <= connections.length <= 10^5
  • connections[i].length == 2
  • 0 <= a, b < n, and a != b
  • There are no repeated connections.

title: Daily Temperatures
statement_html:
Given an array of integers temperatures representing daily temperatures, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you would have to wait after day i to get a warmer temperature.

If there is no future day for which this is possible, keep answer[i] === 0 instead.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= temperatures.length <= 10^5
  • 30 <= temperatures[i] <= 100

title: Decode String
statement_html:
Given an encoded string s, return its decoded string.

The encoding rule is k[encoded_string], meaning the encoded_string inside the square brackets is repeated exactly k times. k is guaranteed to be a positive integer.

You may assume the input string is always valid and does not contain extra spaces; square brackets are well-formed and nesting is allowed, e.g. 3[a2[c]].
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 30
  • s consists of lowercase English letters, digits, and square brackets []
  • The decoded output will have length at most 3 * 10^5

title: Decode Ways
statement_html:
A message containing only uppercase letters A-Z can be encoded to digits using the mapping 'A' -> "1", 'B' -> "2", ..., 'Z' -> "26".

Given a string s containing only digits, return the number of ways it can be decoded into letters. A substring that is "0" by itself is never valid on its own — it must always be paired with the preceding digit to form "10" or "20".
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 100
  • s consists of digit characters only.

title: Delete and Earn
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums. You want to maximize the number of points you get by performing the following operation any number of times:

Pick any nums[i], add it to your points, then remove every element equal to nums[i] - 1 and every element equal to nums[i] + 1 from the array (in addition to removing the chosen element itself).

Return the maximum number of points you can earn by applying this operation some number of times.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4

title: Diagonal Traverse
statement_html:
Given an m x n matrix matrix, return an array of all the elements visited in a diagonal zigzag order.

Start at the top-left corner. Traverse the first diagonal upward toward the top-right, then switch direction and traverse the next diagonal downward toward the bottom-left, alternating directions until every diagonal (from the top-left to the bottom-right corner) has been visited.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 10^4
  • 1 <= m * n <= 10^4
  • -10^5 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^5

title: Distinct Subsequences
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s which equal t.

A subsequence of a string is a new string formed from the original string by deleting some (can be none) of the characters without disturbing the relative positions of the remaining characters.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 1000
  • s and t consist of English letters.

title: Domino and Tromino Tiling
statement_html:
You have two types of tiles: a 2 x 1 domino and an "L" shaped tromino that covers three cells. Both shapes may be rotated.

Given an integer n, return the number of ways to tile a 2 x n board using any number of the two types of tiles. Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

In a tiling, every square must be covered exactly once. Two tilings are different if and only if there exist two 4-directionally adjacent cells covered by two different tiles in one tiling but by the same tile in the other.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 1000

title: Edit Distance
statement_html:
Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2.

You have the following three operations permitted on a word: insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= word1.length, word2.length <= 500
  • word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Employee Free Time
statement_html:
You are given the working schedules of several employees as schedule, where schedule[i] is a list of [start, end] intervals (already sorted and non-overlapping) representing when employee i is busy.

Return a list of finite intervals representing the common, positive-length free time shared by all employees, sorted by start time. Do not include the unbounded free time before the earliest busy interval or after the latest one.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= schedule.length , schedule[i].length <= 50
  • 0 <= start_i < end_i <= 10^8

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement_html:
Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish Notation.

You are given an array of strings tokens representing the expression, where each token is either an integer or one of the operators +, -, *, /. Division between two integers should truncate toward zero.

It is guaranteed that the expression is always valid and evaluates to an integer that fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= tokens.length <= 10^4
  • Each token is either an operator ("+", "-", "*", or "/") or an integer in the range [-200, 200]

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
statement_html:
Spreadsheet programs like Excel label their columns using letters: A, B, C, ..., Z, AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ... and so on.

Given a string columnTitle representing a column's letter label, return the corresponding column number (1-indexed).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= columnTitle.length <= 7
  • columnTitle consists only of uppercase English letters.
  • 1 <= columnNumber <= 2^31 - 1

title: Fibonacci Number
statement_html:
The Fibonacci numbers form a sequence where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1. That is,

F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, and F(n) = F(n - 1) + F(n - 2) for n > 1.

Given n, calculate F(n).
constraints_html: • 0 <= n <= 30

title: Find All Anagrams in a String
statement_html:
Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s. You may return the answer in any order.

An anagram is a rearrangement of the letters of a string that uses every letter exactly once.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length, p.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • s and p consist of lowercase English letters

title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
statement_html:
You are given an array nums of n integers where every nums[i] is in the range [1, n], but some values may be repeated and others may be missing entirely.

Return an array, sorted in ascending order, of all the integers in the range [1, n] that do not appear in nums.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= n

title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
statement_html:
Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order and a value target, find the starting and ending index of the given target.

Return [first, last] where first and last are the indices of the first and last occurrence of target in nums. If target is not present, return [-1, -1].

You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -10^9 <= nums[i], target <= 10^9
  • nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
statement_html:
Suppose an ascending array nums, which may contain duplicate values, was rotated at some unknown pivot, for example [1,2,2,2,3] could become [2,2,3,1,2].

Given the rotated array nums, return the minimum element of the array. Try to minimize the number of comparisons, though duplicates may force O(n) in the worst case.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 5000
  • -5000 <= nums[i] <= 5000

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement_html:
Suppose an ascending, distinct-valued array nums was rotated at some unknown pivot, for example [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] could become [4,5,6,7,0,1,2].

Given the rotated array nums, return the minimum element of the array. Your algorithm should run in O(log n) time.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 5000
  • -5000 <= nums[i] <= 5000
  • All the integers of nums are unique.

title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
statement_html:
There are n cities numbered from 0 to n - 1, connected by weighted, undirected edges[i] = [from_i, to_i, weight_i]. You are also given a distanceThreshold.

For each city, count how many other cities are reachable from it with a shortest path distance of at most distanceThreshold. Return the city with the smallest such count. If there is a tie, return the city with the greatest number.
constraints_html:
• 2 <= n <= 100
  • 1 <= edges.length <= n * (n - 1) / 2
  • 0 <= from_i, to_i < n, and from_i != to_i
  • 1 <= weight_i, distanceThreshold <= 10^4
  • There is at most one edge between any pair of cities.

title: First Missing Positive
statement_html:
Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest missing positive integer (that is, the smallest integer greater than 0 that does not appear anywhere in nums).

Try to design an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) extra space.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1

title: Flood Fill
statement_html:
You are given an image represented as a 2D integer grid image, a starting pixel (sr, sc), and a new color color.

To perform a flood fill, look at the color of the starting pixel, then replace it and every pixel reachable from it via 4-directional (up/down/left/right) moves through pixels of that same original color with color.

Return the modified image after performing the flood fill.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= image.length, image[0].length <= 50
  • 0 <= image[i][j], color < 2^16
  • 0 <= sr < image.length
  • 0 <= sc < image[0].length

title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums and an integer k.

In one operation, you may choose one element of nums and increase it by 1. You may perform this operation at most k times in total (each operation can target any element, and the same element may be chosen more than once).

Return the maximum possible frequency of any single value in the array after performing at most k operations.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
  • 0 <= k <= 10^5

title: Fruit Into Baskets
statement_html:
You are visiting a row of fruit trees represented by the array fruits, where fruits[i] is the type of fruit produced by the i-th tree.

You have exactly two baskets, and each basket can hold an unlimited amount of fruit but only a single type of fruit each. Starting from any tree of your choice, you must pick exactly one piece of fruit from every tree (moving to the right) until you reach a tree that produces a fruit type that wouldn't fit in either basket, at which point you must stop.

Return the maximum number of fruits you can collect this way.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= fruits.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= fruits[i] < fruits.length

title: Gas Station
statement_html:
There are n gas stations arranged in a circle. You are given two integer arrays gas and cost, where gas[i] is the amount of gas at the i-th station and cost[i] is the amount of gas needed to travel from the i-th station to the next one ((i + 1) % n).

You begin the journey with an empty tank at one of the gas stations. Return the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once in the clockwise direction, otherwise return -1. It is guaranteed that if a solution exists, it is unique.
constraints_html:
• n == gas.length == cost.length
  • 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 <= gas[i], cost[i] <= 10^4

title: Graph Valid Tree
statement_html:
You are given an integer n and a list edges where edges[i] = [a, b] represents an undirected edge between nodes a and b, using nodes labeled 0 to n - 1.

Return true if these edges form a valid tree -- meaning every node is reachable from every other node, and there are no cycles.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 2000
  • 0 <= edges.length <= 5000
  • edges[i].length == 2 and there are no self-loops or repeated edges.

title: Group Anagrams
statement_html:
Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the groups in any order, and the strings within a group can be in any order too.

Two strings are anagrams of each other if one can be rearranged (using every letter exactly once) to form the other.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= strs.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100
  • strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Group Shifted Strings
statement_html:
We can shift a lowercase letter to the next letter cyclically, so 'a' becomes 'b', ..., 'y' becomes 'z', and 'z' becomes 'a'. Shifting an entire string means shifting every letter in it by the same amount.

Two strings belong to the same group if one can be obtained from the other by applying some number of shifts (including zero). Given an array of strings strings, group all strings that belong to the same shifting group together.

Return the groups in any order, and the strings within each group in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= strings.length <= 200
  • 1 <= strings[i].length <= 50
  • strings[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
statement_html:
On the i-th minute, exactly customers[i] customers enter a bookstore. All those customers leave at the end of that minute.

On some minutes the owner is grumpy, indicated by grumpy[i] === 1 (otherwise grumpy[i] === 0). When the owner is grumpy, the customers that minute are unsatisfied; otherwise, they are satisfied.

The owner knows a secret technique to keep himself not grumpy for minutes consecutive minutes, but can only use it once.

Return the maximum number of customers that can be satisfied throughout the day.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= minutes <= customers.length == grumpy.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • 0 <= customers[i] <= 1000
  • grumpy[i] is either 0 or 1

title: Hand of Straights
statement_html:
You are given an array of integers hand where hand[i] is the value written on the i-th card, and an integer groupSize.

You want to rearrange the cards into groups so that each group has exactly groupSize cards whose values are consecutive integers, with no gaps.

Return true if it is possible to rearrange all the cards this way, or false otherwise.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= hand.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= hand[i] <= 10^9
  • 1 <= groupSize <= hand.length

title: Happy Number
statement_html:
Write an algorithm to determine whether a positive integer n is a happy number.

Starting from n, repeatedly replace the number with the sum of the squares of its decimal digits. Keep repeating this process. The number is happy if this process eventually reaches 1. If the process instead loops forever in a cycle that never includes 1, the number is not happy.

Return true if n is a happy number, otherwise return false.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1

title: House Robber II
statement_html:
This is the same robbing game as before, except the houses are arranged in a circle: the first house and the last house in nums are now adjacent to each other.

Given nums, return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without robbing two adjacent houses (remembering that the first and last houses count as adjacent).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 100
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000

title: House Robber
statement_html:
You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has some amount of money, given by the array nums. Adjacent houses have connected security systems, so you cannot rob two adjacent houses on the same night without triggering an alarm.

Given nums, return the maximum amount of money you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 100
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 400

title: Insert Interval
statement_html:
You are given an array of non-overlapping intervals intervals, sorted by their start values, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]. You are also given a new interval newInterval = [start, end].

Insert newInterval into intervals so that the result is still sorted by start value and contains no overlapping intervals (merging any that now overlap).

Return the resulting array of intervals.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
  • intervals[i].length == 2 and newInterval.length == 2
  • 0 <= start_i <= end_i <= 10^5

title: Integer Break
statement_html:
Given an integer n, break it into the sum of at least two positive integers and maximize the product of those integers.

Return the maximum product you can achieve.
constraints_html: • 2 <= n <= 58

title: Integer to Roman
statement_html:
Roman numerals use seven symbols: I (1), V (5), X (10), L (50), C (100), D (500), and M (1000). Values are normally written by combining symbols from largest to smallest, left to right.

Six special subtractive pairs are used to avoid four repeated symbols in a row: IV (4), IX (9), XL (40), XC (90), CD (400), and CM (900).

Given an integer num, convert it to its roman numeral representation.
constraints_html: • 1 <= num <= 3999

title: Interleaving String
statement_html:
Given three strings s1, s2, and s3, determine if s3 is formed by an interleaving of s1 and s2.

An interleaving of two strings s and t is a configuration where they are divided into non-empty substrings such that the substrings are concatenated alternately from each string, preserving the original left-to-right order of characters in each of s and t.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 100
  • 0 <= s3.length <= 200
  • s1, s2, and s3 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Interval List Intersections
statement_html:
You are given two lists of closed intervals, firstList and secondList, where firstList[i] = [start_i, end_i] and secondList[j] = [start_j, end_j]. Each list of intervals is pairwise disjoint and sorted in ascending order by start value.

Return the intersection of the two interval lists as an array of intervals (in any order that matches left-to-right, sorted by start). An intersection is the set of points that lie in both an interval from firstList and an interval from secondList; a single shared point (like [3,3]) still counts as a valid intersection.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= firstList.length, secondList.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= start_i <= end_i <= 10^9

title: Is Graph Bipartite
statement_html:
You are given an undirected graph with n nodes labeled 0 to n - 1, represented as an adjacency list graph, where graph[u] lists all nodes adjacent to node u. The graph has no self-loops or repeated edges.

A graph is bipartite if its nodes can be split into two groups such that every edge connects a node in one group to a node in the other (no edge connects two nodes in the same group). Return true if the graph is bipartite.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= graph.length <= 100
  • The graph is undirected and has no self-loops or duplicate edges.

title: Is Subsequence
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, return true if s is a subsequence of t, or false otherwise.

A subsequence of a string is a new string formed by deleting some (possibly zero) characters without disturbing the relative order of the remaining characters. For example, "ace" is a subsequence of "abcde" while "aec" is not.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length <= 100
  • 0 <= t.length <= 10^4
  • s and t consist only of lowercase English letters.

title: Isomorphic Strings
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic.

Two strings are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced (consistently, one character at a time) to obtain t. Every occurrence of a character must map to the same character, and no two different characters may map to the same character, but a character may map to itself.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • t.length == s.length
  • s and t consist of any valid ASCII characters.

title: Jump Game II
statement_html:
You are given a 0-indexed array of integers nums of length n. You are initially positioned at nums[0].

Each element nums[i] represents the maximum length of a forward jump from index i. In other words, if you are at index i, you can jump to any index i + j where 0 <= j <= nums[i] and i + j < n.

Return the minimum number of jumps to reach index n - 1. You may assume it is always possible to reach the last index.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000
  • It is guaranteed that you can reach nums[n - 1].

title: Jump Game III
statement_html:
You are given a zero-indexed array of non-negative integers arr and a starting index start.

When you are at index i, you can jump to either i + arr[i] or i - arr[i], provided that the resulting index stays within the bounds of the array. Jumping outside the array bounds or beyond, is not allowed.

Return true if you can reach any index in arr whose value is 0, starting from start. Otherwise, return false.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= arr.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • 0 <= arr[i] < arr.length
  • 0 <= start < arr.length

title: Jump Game
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums. You are initially positioned at the first index and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position.

Return true if you can reach the last index, or false otherwise.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^5

title: Koko Eating Bananas
statement_html:
Koko loves bananas. There are piles of bananas, with piles[i] bananas in the i-th pile. The guards have gone and will come back in h hours.

Koko decides on an eating speed of k bananas per hour. Each hour, she chooses one pile and eats k bananas from it. If the pile has fewer than k bananas, she eats all of them and does not eat any more bananas during that hour.

Koko wants to eat as slowly as possible while still finishing all the piles before the guards return. Return the minimum integer eating speed k such that she can eat all the bananas within h hours.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= piles.length <= 10^4
  • piles.length <= h <= 10^9
  • 1 <= piles[i] <= 10^9

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.

Note that it is the kth largest element when the array is sorted, not the kth distinct value — duplicates each count as their own element.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= k <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
statement_html:
You are given an n x n matrix matrix where each of the rows and columns is sorted in ascending order.

Return the kth smallest element in the matrix, counting all n2 elements (not just the distinct ones).
constraints_html:
• n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 300
  • -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9
  • Each row and column of matrix is sorted in ascending order.
  • 1 <= k <= n^2

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
statement_html: Given an array of integers heights representing the heights of bars in a histogram, where each bar has a width of 1 and the bars are placed side by side, find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within the histogram.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= heights.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= heights[i] <= 10^4

title: Last Stone Weight
statement_html:
You are given an array of integers stones where each value is the weight of a stone. On each turn, pick up the two heaviest stones and smash them together.

Suppose the two smashed stones have weights x and y with x <= y. If they are equal, both stones are destroyed. Otherwise, the stone of weight x is destroyed and the stone of weight y is replaced by a new stone of weight y - x.

Continue until at most one stone remains, and return that stone's weight, or 0 if no stones are left.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= stones.length <= 30
  • 1 <= stones[i] <= 1000

title: Lemonade Change
statement_html:
Each lemonade costs $5. Customers stand in a line and each buys exactly one lemonade, paying with either a $5, $10, or $20 bill, given in order in the array bills.

You start with no change on hand. For each customer you must give back the correct change so that they net pay exactly $5. You can only use bills you've collected from previous customers to make change (assume you can produce as much change as you'd like from the bills you have on hand).

Return true if you can provide correct change to every customer, otherwise return false.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= bills.length <= 10^5
  • bills[i] is 5, 10, or 20

title: Length of Last Word
statement_html:
Given a string s consisting of words separated by one or more spaces, return the length of the last word in the string.

A word is a maximal substring of non-space characters. The string may contain leading or trailing spaces.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^4
  • s consists of English letters and spaces ' '.
  • There is at least one word in s.

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement_html:
Given an array of strings strs, return the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the array.

If no common prefix exists among all the strings, return an empty string "".
constraints_html:
• 1 <= strs.length <= 200
  • 0 <= strs[i].length <= 200
  • strs[i] consists of only lowercase English letters (if non-empty).

title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement_html:
Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

A subsequence of a string is a new string generated from the original string with some characters (can be none) deleted without changing the relative order of the remaining characters.

A common subsequence of two strings is a subsequence that is common to both strings.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= text1.length, text2.length <= 1000
  • text1 and text2 consist of only lowercase English characters.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement_html:
Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence (a run of integers that each differ from the next by exactly 1).

The elements of the sequence do not need to appear next to each other in the array, and your algorithm should run in O(n) time.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
statement_html:
Given an m x n integer matrix, return the length of the longest strictly increasing path.

From each cell, you may move in any of the four cardinal directions: up, down, left, or right. You may not move diagonally or move outside the boundary of the matrix.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 200
  • 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2^31 - 1

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement_html: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (elements don't need to be contiguous, but must keep their relative order).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 2500
  • -104 <= nums[i] <= 104

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement_html:
You are given a string s consisting of uppercase English letters, and an integer k. You may change up to k characters of s to any other uppercase English letter, any number of times.

Return the length of the longest substring you can obtain that contains only a single repeating letter after performing at most k such changes.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^5
  • s consists of only uppercase English letters.
  • 0 <= k <= s.length

title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
statement_html:
Given a string s and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring of s that contains at most k distinct characters.

If k is 0, no non-empty substring qualifies, so the answer is 0.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= k <= 50
  • s consists of English letters

title: Longest Substring with At Most Two Distinct Characters
statement_html: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most two distinct characters.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^5
  • s consists of English letters

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement_html: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring that does not contain any repeated characters.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • s consists of English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces.

title: Longest Word in Dictionary
statement_html:
Given an array of strings words, find the longest word that can be built one character at a time by other words in words. A word w qualifies only if every one of its non-empty prefixes is also present somewhere in words.

Return the longest qualifying word. If more than one word has the same (longest) length, return the one that is lexicographically smallest. If no word qualifies, return an empty string "".
constraints_html:
• 1 <= words.length <= 1000
  • 1 <= words[i].length <= 30
  • words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Majority Element
statement_html:
Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element — the value that appears more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times.

You may assume the majority element always exists in the array.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 5 * 10^4
  • -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1

title: Max Area of Island
statement_html:
You are given an m x n binary grid grid where 1 represents land and 0 represents water.

An island is a group of 1s connected horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). The area of an island is the number of cells it contains. Return the maximum area of an island in the grid, or 0 if there is no island.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= m, n <= 50
  • grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

title: Max Consecutive Ones III
statement_html:
You are given a binary array nums (containing only 0s and 1s) and an integer k.

You are allowed to flip at most k zeros to ones. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s that you can achieve after doing so.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • nums[i] is either 0 or 1
  • 0 <= k <= nums.length

title: Max Increase to Keep City Skyline
statement_html:
You are given an n x n grid grid where grid[r][c] is the height of a building located at row r and column c.

The skyline of a row (viewed from the left or right side of the grid) is the maximum building height in that row. The skyline of a column (viewed from the front or back) is the maximum building height in that column.

You may increase the height of any building, but the skyline viewed from any of the four directions must not change. Return the maximum total sum by which the heights of all buildings can be increased.
constraints_html:
• n == grid.length == grid[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 50
  • 0 <= grid[r][c] <= 100

title: Maximal Square
statement_html: Given an m x n binary matrix filled with '0's and '1's, find the largest square containing only '1's, and return its area.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 300
  • matrix[i][j] is '0' or '1'.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement_html: Given an integer array nums, find a contiguous, non-empty subarray whose product is the largest, and return that product.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 104
  • -10 <= nums[i] <= 10
  • The product of any subarray fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Maximum Subarray
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum, and return its sum.

A subarray is a contiguous part of an array.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement_html:
You are given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of sizes m and n respectively.

Return the median of the two sorted arrays, as if they had been merged into a single sorted array. Aim for an overall run time complexity of O(log(m+n)).
constraints_html:
• nums1.length == m
  • nums2.length == n
  • 0 <= m, n <= 1000
  • 1 <= m + n <= 2000
  • -10^6 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 10^6

title: Meeting Rooms II
statement_html:
You are given an array of meeting time intervals intervals, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i].

Return the minimum number of conference rooms required so that all the meetings can be held without any two overlapping meetings sharing the same room.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= start_i < end_i <= 10^6

title: Meeting Rooms
statement_html:
You are given an array of meeting time intervals intervals, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i].

Return true if a single person could attend every meeting in the list without any two meetings overlapping in time, or false otherwise.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= start_i < end_i <= 10^6

title: Merge Intervals
statement_html:
Given an array of intervals intervals, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

Two intervals overlap if they share at least one point, meaning touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] should be merged into [1,5].
constraints_html:
• 1 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= start_i <= end_i <= 5 * 10^4

title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
statement_html:
You are given a 2D array triplets, where triplets[i] = [a, b, c] represents the i-th triplet. You are also given an array target = [x, y, z].

You may pick any subset of the triplets (including none) and "merge" them together. Merging two triplets [a, b, c] and [d, e, f] produces a new triplet [max(a,d), max(b,e), max(c,f)]. You may perform this merge operation as many times as you like on any triplets currently available (the originals or previously merged results).

Return true if it is possible to obtain the triplet target as one of the merge results, otherwise return false.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= triplets.length <= 10^5
  • Each triplets[i] and target has exactly 3 integers.
  • 1 <= triplets[i][j], target[j] <= 1000

title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
statement_html:
You are given an integer array cost where cost[i] is the cost of the i-th step on a staircase. Once you pay the cost, you can either climb one or two steps.

You can start climbing from step index 0 or step index 1.

Return the minimum cost to reach the top of the floor, which is one step past the last index in cost.
constraints_html:
• 2 <= cost.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= cost[i] <= 999

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
statement_html:
You are given an array points where points[i] = [x_i, y_i] represents the coordinates of a point on a 2D plane. The cost of connecting two points is the Manhattan distance between them: |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|.

Return the minimum total cost to connect all the points together so that there is exactly one simple path between every pair of points (i.e. build a minimum spanning tree over the points).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= points.length <= 1000
  • -10^6 <= x_i, y_i <= 10^6
  • All pairs (x_i, y_i) are distinct.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
statement_html:
You are given a 2D array intervals, where intervals[i] = [left_i, right_i] describes the i-th interval starting at left_i and ending at right_i (inclusive). The size of an interval is right_i - left_i + 1.

You are also given an array of integers queries. For each queries[j], find the size of the smallest interval that contains queries[j] (that is, left_i <= queries[j] <= right_i). If no interval contains queries[j], the answer for that query is -1.

Return an array of answers, one for each query, in the same order as queries.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= intervals.length <= 1500
  • 1 <= left_i <= right_i <= 10^7
  • 1 <= queries.length <= 1500
  • 1 <= queries[j] <= 10^7

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
statement_html:
There are a number of spherical balloons floating along a wall, each represented as a horizontal diameter by the array points, where points[i] = [x_start, x_end] is the horizontal span covered by the i-th balloon.

An arrow can be shot straight up from any horizontal position, and it bursts every balloon whose span contains that x-coordinate (an arrow at a balloon's exact boundary also bursts it). There is no limit to how far an arrow can travel vertically.

Return the minimum number of arrows needed to burst every balloon.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= points.length <= 10^5
  • -2^31 <= x_start < x_end <= 2^31 - 1

title: Minimum Path Sum
statement_html:
Given an m x n grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner which minimizes the sum of all numbers along its path.

You may only move either down or right at any point in time.
constraints_html:
• m == grid.length
  • n == grid[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 200
  • 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 100

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement_html:
You are given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target.

Find the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to target. If no such subarray exists, return 0 instead.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= target <= 10^9
  • 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, return the shortest substring of s such that every character of t (including repeats) appears in it.

If there is no such substring, return an empty string "".

If there are multiple valid windows of the same shortest length, returning any of them is accepted.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 1000
  • s and t consist of English letters.

title: Missing Number II
statement_html:
You are given an array nums of length n containing n distinct integers, every one of them taken from the range [1, n + 1] (a 1-indexed variant of the classic missing-number setup). Exactly one integer from that range is absent from nums.

Return the missing integer. Try to solve it using O(1) extra space with bitwise operations, without allocating an auxiliary array or set the size of the range.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 10^4
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= n + 1
  • All values in nums are distinct.

title: Missing Number
statement_html: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers taken from the range [0, n], return the one number in that range that is missing from the array.
constraints_html:
• n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 10^4
  • All numbers in nums are unique and in the range [0, n].

title: Multiply Strings
statement_html:
You are given two non-negative integers num1 and num2, each represented as a string of decimal digits. Return the product of num1 and num2, also represented as a string.

The numbers can be arbitrarily large, so you should not convert the entire inputs directly into native numeric types (they may not fit) — compute the product using string/array based digit arithmetic instead.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= num1.length, num2.length <= 200
  • num1 and num2 consist only of digits.
  • Neither num1 nor num2 has leading zeros, unless it is exactly "0".

title: My Calendar I
statement_html:
Imagine a calendar that starts out empty. You are given a list bookings of events, where bookings[i] = [start_i, end_i], presented in the order you must try to add them.

A new event can be added to the calendar only if it does not cause a double booking, meaning it does not overlap with any event already on the calendar. Two events [s1, e1] and [s2, e2] overlap only if s1 < e2 and s2 < e1 — touching at an endpoint (e.g. [5,10] and [10,15]) is fine.

Process the events in bookings in order: for each one, add it to the calendar if possible (permanently, affecting later checks), otherwise skip it. Return an array of booleans, one per event in bookings, indicating whether that event was successfully added.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= bookings.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= start_i < end_i <= 10^9

title: N-Queens II
statement_html:
The n-queens puzzle asks you to place n chess queens on an n x n board so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal).

Given an integer n, return the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle, without needing to construct the boards themselves.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 9

title: Network Delay Time
statement_html:
There are n network nodes labeled from 1 to n. You are given a list of travel times as directed edges times[i] = (u, v, w), meaning a signal sent from node u reaches node v after w time units.

A signal is sent from a starting node k. Return the minimum time it takes for the signal to reach every node in the network. If it is impossible for the signal to reach all n nodes, return -1.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 100
  • 0 <= times.length <= 6000
  • 1 <= u, v <= n, and u != v
  • 0 <= w <= 100
  • 1 <= k <= n

title: Next Greater Element I
statement_html:
You are given two arrays nums1 and nums2, both containing distinct values, where nums1 is a subset of nums2.

For each value nums1[i], find the index of that value in nums2 and find the first element to its right in nums2 that is greater than it (its "next greater element"). If it does not exist, use -1 for that value instead.

Return an array answer of the same length as nums1 such that answer[i] is the next greater element of nums1[i] as described above.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums1.length <= nums2.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 10^4
  • All integers in nums1 and nums2 are unique
  • All integers in nums1 also appear in nums2

title: Next Greater Element II
statement_html:
Given a circular integer array nums (the last element is considered adjacent to the first), return an array answer such that answer[i] is the next greater number for nums[i].

The next greater number of a value x is the first number greater than x found by traversing the array in order, wrapping around to the beginning if needed. If no such number exists, answer[i] should be -1.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
statement_html:
You are given an array of intervals, intervals, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i].

Return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove so that the remaining intervals do not overlap (intervals that merely touch at an endpoint, such as [1,2] and [2,3], are not considered overlapping).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= intervals.length <= 10^5
  • -5 * 10^4 <= start_i < end_i <= 5 * 10^4

title: Number of 1 Bits
statement_html: Given an unsigned 32-bit integer n, return the number of 1 bits it has in its binary representation (this is sometimes called the Hamming weight).
constraints_html: • The input is an unsigned 32-bit integer.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
statement_html:
You are given an integer n and a list edges where edges[i] = [a, b] represents an undirected edge between nodes a and b, using nodes labeled 0 to n - 1.

Return the number of connected components in the graph.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 2000
  • 0 <= edges.length <= 5000
  • There are no self-loops or repeated edges.

title: Number of Distinct Islands
statement_html:
You are given an m x n binary grid grid where 1 represents land and 0 represents water. An island is a group of 1s connected 4-directionally (horizontal or vertical).

Two islands are considered the same shape if one can be translated (shifted up/down/left/right, without rotating or reflecting) to exactly match the other. Return the number of distinct island shapes in the grid.
constraints_html:
• m == grid.length
  • n == grid[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 50
  • grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

title: Number of Islands
statement_html:
You are given an m x n 2D grid made of the characters '1' (land) and '0' (water).

An island is a group of adjacent lands connected horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). Assume all four edges of the grid are surrounded by water. Return the number of islands in the grid.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= m, n <= 300
  • grid[i][j] is '0' or '1'.

title: Number of Provinces
statement_html:
There are n cities. Some are directly connected, and others are not. A province is a group of cities that are connected, directly or indirectly, but not connected to any city outside the group.

You are given an n x n matrix isConnected, where isConnected[i][j] = 1 if the i-th city and the j-th city are directly connected, and 0 otherwise. Return the total number of provinces.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 200
  • isConnected[i][i] == 1
  • isConnected[i][j] == isConnected[j][i]

title: One Edit Distance
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, return true if they are exactly one edit apart, otherwise return false.

An edit on a string is defined as exactly one of the following operations:

  • Insert one character into the string.
  • Delete one character from the string.
  • Replace one character in the string with a different character.

    • Two identical strings are considered zero edits apart, so they should return false.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length, t.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • s and t consist of lowercase English letters, digits, or spaces.

title: Palindrome Number
statement_html:
Given an integer x, return true if x reads the same forwards and backwards (a palindrome), and false otherwise.

Negative numbers are never palindromes, since the minus sign would need to appear on both ends.

title: Palindromic Substrings
statement_html:
Given a string s, return the number of substrings of s that are palindromes (read the same forwards and backwards).

Substrings that occur at different starting or ending positions are counted separately, even if the resulting text is the same.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 1000
  • s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
statement_html: Given an integer array nums, return true if it can be split into two subsets whose elements sum to the same value.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 200
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 100

title: Partition Labels
statement_html:
You are given a string s consisting only of lowercase English letters. Split s into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part, while using every character of s exactly once across the parts (each part is a contiguous substring).

Return an array of integers representing the size of each part, in the order the parts occur in s.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 500
  • s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Pascal's Triangle
statement_html:
Given an integer numRows, return the first numRows rows of Pascal's triangle.

In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it (and the first and last number of every row is 1).
constraints_html: • 1 <= numRows <= 30

title: Perfect Squares
statement_html:
Given an integer n, return the fewest number of perfect square numbers that sum up to n.

A perfect square is an integer that is the square of another integer, for example 1, 4, 9, and 16 are perfect squares while 3 and 11 are not.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 10^4

title: Permutation in String
statement_html:
Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring, or false otherwise.

In other words, determine whether some rearrangement of the characters of s1 appears as a substring inside s2.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 10^4
  • s1 and s2 consist only of lowercase English letters.

title: Plus One
statement_html:
You are given a non-empty array of integers digits representing a large, non-negative integer. Each element holds a single digit, and the digits are ordered from most significant to least significant. The integer does not contain any leading zeros, except for the number 0 itself.

Add one to the number represented by digits, and return the resulting array of digits.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= digits.length <= 100
  • 0 <= digits[i] <= 9
  • digits does not contain any leading zero, except for the number 0 itself.

title: Power of Four
statement_html:
Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of four, and false otherwise.

An integer n is a power of four if there exists an integer x such that n == 4^x. As a bonus challenge, try solving it without using loops or recursion, using only bitwise tricks.

title: Power of Two
statement_html:
Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two, and false otherwise.

An integer n is a power of two if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x. Try to solve this in O(1) time using a bitwise trick rather than a loop.

title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
statement_html:
You are given an array of people attending a queue, people, where people[i] = [h_i, k_i] means the i-th person has height h_i, and there are exactly k_i other people in front of them who have a height greater than or equal to h_i.

Reconstruct and return the queue, represented as an array of the same [h, k] pairs in the valid order, such that every person's k value is satisfied.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= people.length <= 2000
  • 0 <= h_i <= 10^6
  • 0 <= k_i < people.length

title: Ransom Note
statement_html:
Given two strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed by cutting out and rearranging individual letters from magazine, or false otherwise.

Each letter available in magazine can be used at most once when building ransomNote.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= ransomNote.length, magazine.length <= 10^5
  • ransomNote and magazine consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
statement_html:
You are given a list of airline tickets where tickets[i] = [from, to] represents a flight departing from airport from and arriving at airport to. Reconstruct the itinerary, starting from "JFK", that uses every ticket exactly once.

If more than one valid itinerary exists, return the one that is lexicographically smallest when read as a sequence of airport codes. You may assume all tickets form at least one valid itinerary that starts at "JFK" and uses every ticket.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= tickets.length <= 300
  • Every airport code consists of three uppercase English letters.
  • All tickets, together, form at least one valid itinerary starting at JFK.

title: Redundant Connection
statement_html:
A tree with n nodes labeled 1 to n has exactly n - 1 edges connecting every node. You are given edges, a list of n undirected edges (one more than a tree needs) where edges[i] = [a, b]. Adding this extra edge to an otherwise valid tree created exactly one cycle.

Return the edge that can be removed so that the remaining edges form a tree on all n nodes. If several edges could be removed, return the one that occurs last in the input array edges.
constraints_html:
• n == edges.length, 3 <= n <= 1000
  • edges[i].length == 2
  • 1 <= a, b <= n

title: Regular Expression Matching
statement_html:
Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement regular expression matching that supports '.' and '*' where:

'.' matches any single character, and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element.

The matching should cover the entire input string (not partial).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 20
  • 1 <= p.length <= 20
  • s contains only lowercase English letters.
  • p contains only lowercase English letters, '.', and '*'.
  • It is guaranteed for each appearance of the character '*', there will be a previous valid character to match.

title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
statement_html:
You are given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters. A duplicate removal operation picks two adjacent and equal letters and removes both of them.

Repeatedly perform duplicate removal operations on s until no more can be made. Return the final resulting string. It is guaranteed the answer is unique.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^5
  • s consists only of lowercase English letters

title: Remove Covered Intervals
statement_html:
You are given an array of closed intervals intervals, where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]. An interval [s1, e1] is considered covered by another interval [s2, e2] if s2 <= s1 and e1 <= e2.

Remove every interval that is covered by another interval in the list, and return the number of intervals that remain.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= intervals.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= start_i < end_i <= 5 * 10^4
  • All the intervals are unique

title: Repeated Substring Pattern
statement_html: Given a string s, return true if it can be constructed by taking some substring of it and repeating that substring multiple times (two or more) end-to-end to form the whole of s. Otherwise return false.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^4
  • s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Replace Words
statement_html:
In English, a root word can have many words built from it by adding a suffix, for example the root "help" can form "helped", "helping", and "helpful".

You are given a list of root words dictionary and a sentence (a string of lowercase words separated by single spaces). For every word in the sentence, if it can be formed by adding a suffix onto one of the roots, replace it with the shortest matching root. If a word matches no root, leave it unchanged.

Return the sentence after all replacements have been made.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= dictionary.length <= 1000
  • 1 <= dictionary[i].length <= 100
  • dictionary[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
  • 1 <= sentence.length <= 10^6
  • sentence consists of lowercase English letters and single spaces, with no leading or trailing spaces.
