title: Reshape the Matrix
statement_html:
You are given a 2D array mat with m rows and n columns, and two integers r and c representing the desired number of rows and columns for a new reshaped matrix.

The reshaped matrix should be filled with all the elements of mat in the same left-to-right, top-to-bottom row order as the original.

If the reshape operation is impossible (the total number of elements r * c does not equal m * n), return the original matrix mat unchanged. Otherwise, return the reshaped r x c matrix.
constraints_html:
• m == mat.length, n == mat[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 100
  • -1000 <= mat[i][j] <= 1000
  • 1 <= r, c <= 300

title: Reverse Bits
statement_html: Given a 32-bit unsigned integer n, return the unsigned integer obtained by reversing the bits of its 32-bit binary representation.
constraints_html: • The input is a binary string of length exactly 32 interpreted as an unsigned integer.

title: Reverse Vowels of a String
statement_html:
Given a string s, reverse only the vowel characters within it ('a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u', in either upper or lower case, and each may appear more than once), and return the result.

Consonants and every other character must stay in their original positions.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^5
  • s consists of printable ASCII characters.

title: Roman to Integer
statement_html:
Roman numerals use seven symbols: I (1), V (5), X (10), L (50), C (100), D (500), and M (1000). Symbol values are normally added together from left to right (e.g. II is 2, XIII is 13).

As a special case, when a smaller-value symbol appears immediately before a larger-value symbol, its value is subtracted instead: IV is 4, IX is 9, XL is 40, XC is 90, CD is 400, and CM is 900.

Given a valid roman numeral string s, convert it to its integer value.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 15
  • s contains only the characters ('I','V','X','L','C','D','M').
  • s is a valid roman numeral representing an integer in the range [1, 3999].

title: Rotate Image
statement_html:
You are given an n x n 2D array matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise.

You may rotate matrix in place if you want, but your function must return the resulting rotated matrix.
constraints_html:
• n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 20
  • -1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000

title: Rotting Oranges
statement_html:
You are given an m x n grid of integers representing a box of oranges, where 0 is an empty cell, 1 is a fresh orange, and 2 is a rotten orange.

Every minute, any fresh orange that is adjacent (up, down, left, or right) to a rotten orange also becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes that must pass until no fresh orange remains. If that is impossible, return -1.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= m, n <= 10
  • grid[i][j] is 0, 1, or 2.

title: Search a 2D Matrix II
statement_html:
You are given an m x n integer matrix matrix with the following properties:

  • Every row is sorted in increasing order from left to right.
  • Every column is sorted in increasing order from top to bottom.

    • Given an integer target, return true if target is somewhere in matrix, or false otherwise. Note that unlike a fully row-major sorted matrix, the last element of one row is not guaranteed to be smaller than the first element of the next row.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 300
  • -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9
  • -10^9 <= target <= 10^9

title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement_html:
Write an efficient algorithm that searches for a value in an m x n matrix. This matrix has the following properties:

  • Integers in each row are sorted from left to right.
  • The first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row.

    • Given matrix, an m x n matrix, and target, return true if target is in the matrix, and false otherwise.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 100
  • -104 <= matrix[i][j], target <= 104

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums, sorted in ascending order but possibly containing duplicate values, which has possibly been rotated at some unknown pivot.

Given the rotated array nums and an integer target, return true if target exists in nums, or false otherwise.

Because duplicates are allowed, you cannot always guarantee O(log n) runtime, but your solution should still avoid a plain linear scan whenever possible.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 5000
  • -10^4 <= nums[i], target <= 10^4
  • nums is guaranteed to be sorted and then possibly rotated.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums, sorted in ascending order with distinct values, that has possibly been rotated at some unknown pivot.

For example, [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] might become [4,5,6,7,0,1,2] after being rotated.

Given the rotated array nums and an integer target, return the index of target if it exists in nums, or -1 if it does not. Your algorithm should run in O(log n) time.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 5000
  • Every value in nums is unique.
  • nums is an ascending array that has possibly been rotated.
  • -10^4 <= target, nums[i] <= 10^4

title: Search Insert Position
statement_html:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers nums and a target value target, return the index of target if it is found in the array.

If target is not found, return the index where it would be inserted to keep nums sorted in ascending order.

You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
  • nums contains distinct values sorted in ascending order.
  • -10^4 <= target <= 10^4

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
statement_html:
Given an n x n binary grid grid, find the length of the shortest clear path from the top-left cell (0, 0) to the bottom-right cell (n - 1, n - 1).

A clear path consists only of cells with value 0, and consecutive cells in the path must be connected 8-directionally (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally adjacent). The length of a path is the number of visited cells, including the start and end cells.

If the starting cell or ending cell is not 0, or no such path exists, return -1.
constraints_html:
• n == grid.length == grid[i].length
  • 1 <= n <= 100
  • grid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

title: Simplify Path
statement_html:
You are given an absolute Unix-style file path path as a string, and you must transform it into its simplified canonical path.

In a Unix-style path, a single period . refers to the current directory, a double period .. refers to the parent directory (moving up one level, or staying at the root if already there), and multiple consecutive slashes are treated as a single slash.

The canonical path should start with a single slash, directories should be separated by exactly one slash, it should not end with a trailing slash (unless it is the root /), and it should not contain . or .. segments.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= path.length <= 3000
  • path starts with a single slash /
  • path consists of English letters, digits, ., /, or _
  • path is a valid absolute Unix path

title: Single Number II
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums where every element appears exactly three times except for one element which appears only once, find and return that single element.

Your algorithm should run in linear time and use only constant extra space.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1
  • Every element appears exactly three times except for one.

title: Single Number IV
statement_html:
You are given a non-empty array of integers nums where every element appears exactly twice, except for a single element that appears exactly once. Find and return that element.

Your solution should run in O(n) time while using only O(1) extra space — think about what happens when you XOR every number in the array together.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • -3 * 10^4 <= nums[i] <= 3 * 10^4
  • Every element appears exactly twice except for one element which appears exactly once.

title: Single Number
statement_html:
Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears exactly twice except for one element which appears only once.

Find and return that single element. Your algorithm should run in linear time and use only constant extra space.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • -3 * 10^4 <= nums[i] <= 3 * 10^4
  • Every element appears twice except for one.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement_html:
You are given an array of integers nums and an integer k representing the size of a sliding window that moves from the very left of the array to the very right, one position at a time.

Return an array of the maximum value in the window at each position it stops at.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 105
  • 1 <= k <= nums.length

title: Spiral Matrix II
statement_html:
Given a positive integer n, generate an n x n matrix filled with the numbers 1 to n^2 in spiral order: starting at the top-left corner, moving right across the top row, down the right column, left across the bottom row, up the left column, and spiraling inward.

Return the generated matrix.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 20

title: Spiral Matrix
statement_html: Given an m x n 2D array matrix, return all elements of matrix in spiral order: starting at the top-left corner, moving right across the top row, down the right column, left across the bottom row, up the left column, and spiraling inward until every element has been visited.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length, n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 10
  • -100 <= matrix[i][j] <= 100

title: Split Array Largest Sum
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums and an integer m, split nums into m non-empty contiguous subarrays.

Design a split that minimizes the largest sum among these m subarrays, and return that minimized largest sum.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^6
  • 1 <= m <= min(50, nums.length)

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
statement_html: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number, itself sorted in non-decreasing order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
  • nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: String to Integer (atoi)
statement_html:
Implement a function myAtoi(s) that converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer, following the same general algorithm as the C/C++ atoi function:

  • Skip any leading whitespace characters.
  • An optional '+' or '-' sign may follow, determining the result's sign (assume positive if absent).
  • Read in as many consecutive digit characters as possible to form the numeric value; stop at the first non-digit character (or the end of the string). If no digits were read, the result is 0.
  • Clamp the result so it fits within the 32-bit signed integer range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1]. Values below the range become -2^31, and values above become 2^31 - 1.

    • Return the resulting integer.
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length <= 200
  • s consists of English letters, digits, spaces, '+', '-', and '.'.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the total number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to exactly k.

A subarray is a contiguous, non-empty run of elements. Elements can be negative, positive, or zero.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000
  • -10^7 <= k <= 10^7

title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays that contain exactly k different integers.

For example, [1,2,1,2,3] has 3 good subarrays with exactly 1 different integer: [1], [2], [1].
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4
  • 1 <= nums[i], k <= nums.length

title: Subsets II
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums that may contain duplicate values, return every possible subset (the power set), without any subset appearing more than once.

The subsets may be returned in any order, and the elements within each subset may be in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10
  • -10 <= nums[i] <= 10

title: Subsets
statement_html:
Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return every possible subset (the power set), including the empty subset and nums itself.

The subsets may be returned in any order, and the elements within each subset may be in any order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10
  • -10 <= nums[i] <= 10
  • All elements of nums are unique.

title: Sum of Two Integers
statement_html:
Given two integers a and b, return their sum — but you may not use the + or - operators anywhere in your solution.

Instead, use bitwise operations: XOR two numbers to add them without carrying, and AND plus a left shift to compute the carry that still needs to be added in. Repeat until there is no carry left. Handle negative numbers correctly by working in 32-bit two's complement.
constraints_html: • -1000 <= a, b <= 1000

title: Swim in Rising Water
statement_html:
You are given an n x n grid where grid[i][j] is the elevation at position (i, j). Rain starts to fall, and at time t the depth of water everywhere is t. You may swim from a square to an adjacent 4-directional square only if both squares have elevation <= t.

You start at the top-left square (0, 0). Return the least time t such that you can reach the bottom-right square (n - 1, n - 1).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= n <= 50
  • 0 <= grid[i][j] < n * n
  • Each value in grid is unique.

title: Target Sum
statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums and an integer target.

You want to build an expression out of nums by adding one of the symbols '+' or '-' before each integer in nums and then concatenate all the integers.

For example, if nums = [2, 1], you can add a '+' before 2 and a '-' before 1 and concatenate them to build the expression "+2-1".

Return the number of different expressions that you can build which evaluate to target.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 20
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000
  • 0 <= sum(nums[i]) <= 1000
  • -1000 <= target <= 1000

title: Task Scheduler
statement_html:
You are given an array of characters tasks representing tasks a CPU needs to run, and a non-negative integer n, the required cooldown between two occurrences of the same task.

Each unit of time the CPU can either complete one task or sit idle. The same type of task may only be run again once at least n units of time have passed since it last ran.

Return the minimum number of time units needed to finish all the given tasks.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= tasks.length <= 10^4
  • tasks[i] is an uppercase English letter.
  • 0 <= n <= 100

title: Text Justification
statement_html:
Given an array of strings words and a target line width maxWidth, format the text so it is fully (left and right) justified.

Greedily pack as many words as possible onto each line: a word can be added to the current line as long as the line (with a single space between each word so far) does not exceed maxWidth characters.

For every line except the last, distribute the extra spaces between words as evenly as possible so the line is exactly maxWidth characters wide. If the spaces cannot be split evenly, the leftmost gaps get one extra space each. If a line contains only one word, pad it with trailing spaces to reach maxWidth.

The last line should be left-justified with a single space between words, then padded with trailing spaces so it is exactly maxWidth characters wide.

Return the resulting lines as an array of strings.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= words.length <= 300
  • 1 <= words[i].length <= 20
  • words[i] consists of non-space characters only.
  • 1 <= maxWidth <= 100
  • words[i].length <= maxWidth

title: Toeplitz Matrix
statement_html:
A matrix is called a Toeplitz matrix if every diagonal that runs from the top-left to the bottom-right has the same elements.

Given an m x n matrix matrix, return true if it is a Toeplitz matrix, otherwise return false.
constraints_html:
• m == matrix.length
  • n == matrix[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 20
  • 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 99

title: Top K Frequent Words
statement_html:
Given an array of strings words and an integer k, return the k most frequent strings.

Order the result by frequency from highest to lowest. If two words have the same frequency, order them lexicographically (alphabetically ascending).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= words.length <= 500
  • 1 <= words[i].length <= 10
  • words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
  • k is between 1 and the number of distinct words.

title: Total Hamming Distance
statement_html:
The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of positions at which their binary representations differ.

Given an integer array nums, return the sum of the Hamming distances between every pair of numbers in the array (each unordered pair counted once).

A brute-force double loop works but is O(n^2); for a faster approach, consider counting, for each bit position, how many numbers have a 0 versus a 1 there.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
  • The answer fits within a 32-bit integer.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement_html: Given n non-negative integers in an array height, where each value represents the height of a bar with width 1, compute how much water the terrain can trap after raining.
constraints_html:
• n == height.length
  • 0 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 10^5

title: Two City Scheduling
statement_html:
A company is flying 2n people to two cities, city A and city B, and wants to send exactly n people to each city.

The cost of flying the i-th person to city A is costs[i][0], and to city B is costs[i][1].

Return the minimum total cost to fly everyone so that exactly n people arrive in each city.
constraints_html:
• 2n == costs.length, where n >= 1
  • 2 <= costs.length <= 100, and costs.length is even
  • 1 <= costs[i][0], costs[i][1] <= 1000

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement_html:
Given a 1-indexed array of integers numbers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number.

Return the indices of the two numbers, index1 and index2, added by one, as an integer array [index1, index2] of length 2, where 1 <= index1 < index2 <= numbers.length.

You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
constraints_html:
• 2 <= numbers.length <= 3 * 10^4
  • -1000 <= numbers[i] <= 1000
  • numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order.
  • Exactly one valid answer exists.

title: Two Sum
statement_html:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use thesame element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
constraints_html:
• 2 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10
  • -10 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10
  • -10 ≤ target ≤ 10
  • Only one valid answer exists.

title: Ugly Number II
statement_html:
An ugly number is a positive integer whose only prime factors are 2, 3, and 5. By convention, 1 is considered an ugly number.

Given an integer n, return the nth ugly number, counting them in increasing order.
constraints_html: • 1 <= n <= 1690

title: Unique Paths II
statement_html:
You are given an m x n integer grid obstacleGrid representing a grid where a robot starts at the top-left corner and wants to reach the bottom-right corner. The robot can only move down or right at any point in time.

Some cells contain obstacles, marked as 1 in the grid, while free cells are marked as 0. The robot cannot step onto a cell containing an obstacle.

Return the number of possible unique paths that the robot can take to reach the bottom-right corner.
constraints_html:
• m == obstacleGrid.length
  • n == obstacleGrid[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 100
  • obstacleGrid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

title: Unique Paths III
statement_html:
You are given a 2D grid of integers with four possible values:

  • 1 marks the single starting square.
  • 2 marks the single ending square.
  • 0 marks a walkable empty square.
  • -1 marks an obstacle that cannot be walked on.

Starting at the 1 square, return the number of distinct paths that walk over every non-obstacle square exactly once and finish on the 2 square. You may move up, down, left, or right, and may never revisit a square or step on an obstacle.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= grid.length, grid[i].length <= 20
  • grid[i][j] is -1, 0, 1, or 2.
  • There is exactly one starting square and exactly one ending square.

title: Unique Paths
statement_html:
A robot is located at the top-left corner of an m x n grid. The robot can only move either down or right at any point in time. The robot is trying to reach the bottom-right corner of the grid.

Given the two integers m and n, return the number of possible unique paths that the robot can take to reach the bottom-right corner.
constraints_html: • 1 <= m, n <= 100

title: Valid Anagram
statement_html:
Given two strings s and t, determine whether t is an anagram of s.

A string is an anagram of another if it uses exactly the same characters, the same number of times, just possibly rearranged into a different order.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length, t.length <= 5 * 10^4
  • s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Valid Palindrome
statement_html:
Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome after the following processing: convert all uppercase letters to lowercase, and remove all characters that are not letters or digits.

An empty string (after processing) is considered a valid palindrome.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 2 * 10^5
  • s consists only of printable ASCII characters.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: Valid Parentheses
statement_html:
Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if:

  • Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets.
  • Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
  • Every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 104
  • s consists of parentheses only '()[]{}'.

title: Valid Parenthesis String
statement_html:
Given a string s containing only the characters '(', ')' and '*', determine if s is valid.

A string is considered valid if it is possible to interpret every '*' as either a '(', a ')', or an empty string, such that the resulting string is a valid parentheses sequence (every open bracket is closed in the correct order).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 100
  • s[i] is '(', ')' or '*'

title: Wildcard Matching
statement_html:
Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement wildcard pattern matching that supports '?' and '*' where:

'?' matches any single character, and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including the empty sequence).

The matching should cover the entire input string (not partial).
constraints_html:
• 0 <= s.length, p.length <= 2000
  • s contains only lowercase English letters.
  • p contains only lowercase English letters, '?', or '*'.

title: Word Break
statement_html: Given a string s and a list of strings wordDict, return true if s can be split into a sequence of one or more words from wordDict placed one after another (words may be reused any number of times).
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 300
  • 1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000
  • All strings consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Word Ladder
statement_html:
You are given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a wordList of allowed words. A transformation sequence starts at beginWord, changes exactly one letter at a time to produce a new word, and each intermediate word (including the final one) must appear in wordList. beginWord does not need to be in wordList.

Return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, or 0 if no such sequence exists.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= beginWord.length <= 10, all words have the same length.
  • 1 <= wordList.length <= 5000
  • beginWord != endWord and all words in wordList are distinct.
  • All words consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Word Pattern
statement_html:
You are given a pattern string pattern and a string s containing words separated by single spaces. Determine if s follows the same pattern.

"Follows" here means there is a full bijection (one-to-one mapping in both directions) between each character in pattern and each word in s: the same character always maps to the same word, and the same word always maps to the same character.
constraints_html:
• 1 <= pattern.length <= 300
  • pattern consists of lowercase English letters.
  • 1 <= s.length <= 3000
  • s consists of lowercase English letters and single spaces, with no leading or trailing spaces.

title: Word Search
statement_html:
Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word can be traced out by moving between horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, and false otherwise.

The same grid cell may not be used more than once within a single word's path.
constraints_html:
• m == board.length
  • n == board[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 6
  • 1 <= word.length <= 15
  • board and word consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters.

title: Zigzag Conversion
statement_html:
Given a string s, write it out in a zigzag pattern across numRows rows: starting top-to-bottom down the first column, then diagonally up-and-right to the top of the next column, and so on, repeating this down-then-diagonal-up movement across the whole string.

For example, writing "PAYPALISHIRING" with numRows = 3 produces:

P   A   H   N
A P L S I I G
Y   I   R

Then return the string formed by reading the rows one at a time, from top to bottom, left to right: "PAHNAPLSIIGYIR".
constraints_html:
• 1 <= s.length <= 1000
  • s consists of English letters, punctuation, and spaces.
  • 1 <= numRows <= 1000
